name: gdi
description: {@link window.DrawMode DrawMode}-aware graphics facade. With {@link window.DrawMode} set to 0 its resource factories use GDI+; with {@link window.DrawMode} set to 1 they create the corresponding Direct2D resources instead. A Worker uses the {@link window.DrawMode DrawMode} captured when that Worker is created, so the same gdi.* calls match the parent panel graphics backend.

name: Brush
description:
Creates a drawing brush of the specified type. The meaning of the brush's input parameters depends on its type.
For type == {@link module:Flags.BrushType BrushType.Solid}:
- param1: brush colour in ARGB
For type == {@link module:Flags.BrushType BrushType.LinearGradient}:
- param1: start point coords of linear gradient in form of Array(2) (for ex.: [0, 0])
- param2: end point coords of linear gradient in form of Array(2) (for ex.: [100, 0])
- param3: gradient stops specified as an array with alternating position and color values for each stop (for ex.: [0.0, 0xFF000000, 0.5, 0xFFFF0000, 1.0, 0xFFFFFFFF])
- param4: wrap mode responsible for how the gradient is repeated when drawing. See {@link module:Flags.BrushWrapMode BrushWrapMode}. Default is {@link module:Flags.BrushWrapMode BrushWrapMode.Tile}
For type == {@link module:Flags.BrushType BrushType.RadialGradient}:
- param1: center point coords of radial gradient in form of Array(2) (for ex.: [50, 50])
- param2: radius values for X and Y axes in form of Array(2) (for ex.: [50, 50])
- param3: gradient stops specified as an array with alternating position and color values for each stop (for ex.: [0.0, 0xFF000000, 0.5, 0xFFFF0000, 1.0, 0xFFFFFFFF])
- param4: wrap mode responsible for how the gradient is repeated when drawing. See {@link module:Flags.BrushWrapMode BrushWrapMode}. Default is {@link module:Flags.BrushWrapMode BrushWrapMode.Tile}
For type == {@link module:Flags.BrushType BrushType.Bitmap}:
- param1: {@link GdiBitmap GdiBitmap} object used for drawing by brush
- param2: wrap mode responsible for how the image is repeated when drawing. See {@link module:Flags.BrushWrapMode BrushWrapMode}

returns.description: Brush object used in Draw/Fill methods

throws.description: If the brush parameters are invalid, including malformed points, radius values, gradient stops, or bitmap input.

returns.description: null if was an error (for example pixelData array length is not suitable for the specified parameters)

name: GetWaveformAsync
description:
Decodes an audio track asynchronously and returns a fixed-size waveform amplitude envelope.
Each element of the returned Float32Array is a linear amplitude value in the range 0.0..1.0 for the corresponding part of the requested time range.
Each output point represents one time interval. The interval is divided into up to 8 local windows; for each non-empty window, the peak absolute sample value across all channels is measured, and those local peaks are averaged to produce the output value. This preserves short transients while avoiding the dense appearance produced by taking a single maximum peak over the entire output interval.
Values are not normalized to the loudest point of the track, so their amplitudes remain relative to the decoded audio signal.
Decoding uses one sequential decoder pass. Decoded PCM data is not exposed to JavaScript.

If on_progress is supplied, finalized contiguous ranges of the output envelope are delivered while decoding is still in progress. The callback receives a Float32Array containing the new values and the zero-based output index where that range begins. Progress chunk size and delivery frequency are implementation details and must not be relied on.
For waveform UIs that should appear while decoding, this progressive form is the recommended approach. Use one {@link utils.GetWaveformAsync GetWaveformAsync} call for the whole requested range instead of splitting the track into repeated range calls. One decoder remains open for the sequential pass, avoiding repeated open/seek/decode overhead. For visually smooth rendering, store progress chunks immediately but animate a separate visible front toward the loaded front rather than exposing the native chunk boundaries directly.
Return false from on_progress to cancel the native decode. This is recommended when a progressive request becomes obsolete, for example after the focused or playing track changes. Cancellation rejects the returned Promise. Any other return value continues decoding.
The Promise still resolves with the complete Float32Array when decoding finishes normally, whether or not a progress callback is used.

If duration is 0, the requested range extends from start to the end of the track. If the track length cannot be determined, a non-zero duration must be specified.
A range that extends past a known track end is clipped. If start is at or beyond the known track end, a zero-filled array is returned.
Decoder or input-opening failures reject the returned Promise.

params.name: points
params.description: Number of output points. Valid range: 1..65536.

params.name: start
params.description: Start position in seconds. Must be finite and non-negative.

params.name: duration
params.description: Duration in seconds. Must be finite and non-negative. 0 means from start to the end of the track.

params.name: on_progress
params.description: Optional progress callback. Receives (values, start_index). Return false to cancel decoding.

returns.description: Promise resolved with exactly points linear amplitude values.

throws.description: If handle is null; points, start, or duration is invalid; or on_progress is not a function, null, or undefined.

examples:
<caption>Decode a complete waveform</caption>
const handle = fb.GetNowPlaying();
if (handle) {
    utils.GetWaveformAsync(handle, 2048)
        .then(waveform => {
            console.log(`Decoded ${waveform.length} waveform points`);
        })
        .catch(e => console.log(`GetWaveformAsync failed: ${e}`));
}

<caption>Recommended progressive UI pattern</caption>
let requestId = 0;
let waveform = null;
let loaded = 0;
let visible = 0;
let producerRate = 0;
let lastFrame = 0;

const revealTimer = setInterval(() => {
    if (!waveform || producerRate <= 0) return;

    const now = performance.now();
    const dt = lastFrame ? now - lastFrame : 0;
    lastFrame = now;

    // Smoothly follow what the decoder has really produced. Do not predict
    // completion time from track duration and do not draw chunk boundaries directly.
    visible = Math.min(loaded, visible + producerRate * dt);
    window.Repaint();
}, 16);

async function loadFocusedWaveform() {
    const id = ++requestId;
    const handle = fb.GetFocusItem();
    if (!handle) return;

    const points = 2048;
    const started = performance.now();
    waveform = new Float32Array(points);
    loaded = 0;
    visible = 0;
    producerRate = 0;
    lastFrame = 0;

    try {
        const complete = await utils.GetWaveformAsync(handle, points, 0, 0, (values, start) => {
            if (id !== requestId) return false; // cancel the obsolete native decode

            waveform.set(values, start);
            loaded = Math.max(loaded, start + values.length);

            const elapsed = performance.now() - started;
            if (elapsed > 0) producerRate = loaded / elapsed;
            return true;
        });

        if (id !== requestId) return;
        waveform = complete;
        loaded = complete.length;
    } catch (e) {
        if (id === requestId) console.log(`GetWaveformAsync failed: ${e}`);
    }
}

// See "Focus Track Waveform.js" for a complete rendering example.

name: LoadFont
description: Loads a font file for private use by the current foobar2000 process. The font is not installed in Windows and is not made available to other processes. After a successful call the font becomes available to the foobar2000 process. It can be used by {@link gdi.Font} and {@link d2d.Font} and is visible to other JSplitter panels and Workers. The font is registered privately for the foobar2000 process rather than for JSplitter alone. As a result, it may also become available to native foobar2000 UI and other components that use the Windows font APIs, depending on when they enumerate or create their fonts. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}. The file is registered (cached) once by its normalised absolute path. Calling {@link utils.LoadFont LoadFont} again with the same file returns true without registering it again. Loaded fonts remain available for the lifetime of the foobar2000 process; there is no corresponding unload operation. A font may expose different legacy/GDI and typographic/DirectWrite family names. {@link utils.CheckFont CheckFont} can be used to verify a family name after loading, while {@link utils.ListFonts ListFonts} shows the names reported by the GDI and DirectWrite backends.

params.name: path

returns.description: true if the font is already loaded or was loaded successfully; false if the file does not exist, cannot be read as a font, contains no usable family, or cannot be registered.

name: OpenBinaryReader
description:
Opens a binary file for incremental reading into a caller-provided Uint8Array.
The buffer is reused by the caller, so repeated reads do not allocate a new typed array for every chunk. This is intended for large files or other cases where whole-file {@link utils.ReadBinaryFile ReadBinaryFile} would be inefficient.
Reading is synchronous. For one-shot large-file processing, use the reader inside {@link Worker.RunAsync}; for persistent pipelines, use it from a {@link Worker}. Both approaches keep blocking file I/O off the panel UI thread.
Ordinary read failures are reported through {@link BinaryReader#Read Read} and {@link BinaryReader#EOF EOF}>; they are not thrown as exceptions. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}.

returns.description: Open streaming reader, or null if the reader could not be created. Ordinary file open/setup failures are reported as null, not exceptions.

name: OpenBinaryWriter
description: Opens a binary file for incremental writing from a caller-provided Uint8Array. The file is created or truncated when opened. The parent folder must already exist. Reusing the same typed array avoids allocating temporary buffers for every chunk. Write, flush, and close failures are reported through boolean return values. Writing is synchronous. For long-running processing, use the writer from a {@link Worker} to avoid blocking the panel UI. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}.

returns.description: Open streaming writer, or null if the writer could not be created. Ordinary file creation/open failures are reported as null, not exceptions.

name: OpenDatabase
description:
Opens or creates a SQLite database for synchronous read/write access by given filename.
The special filename :memory: creates an in-memory SQLite database and is not path-resolved. The parent folder of a file-backed database must already exist.
Database work is synchronous, so large imports or expensive queries should be run from a {@link Worker} to avoid blocking the panel UI thread.
SQL values should be passed through the optional parameter array instead of being concatenated into the SQL text. Supported parameter types are null, boolean, number, string, ArrayBuffer, and typed-array views. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}.

params.name: filename
params.description: Absolute or script-relative database filename, or :memory:.

returns.description: Open database handle, or null if the database could not be opened or created. Ordinary open/create failures are reported as null, matching the other Open* resource factories. SQL and database-operation errors after a successful open are reported as exceptions.

name: OpenTextReader
description:
Opens a text file for incremental, line-by-line reading.
Unlike {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}, the whole file is not materialized as one JavaScript string. This makes it suitable for processing large text files incrementally, one line at a time, without requiring the entire file contents to fit in the JavaScript heap.
{@link TextReader#ReadLine ReadLine} removes the line terminator. A return value of null means that no next line could be returned; in that case, {@link TextReader#EOF EOF} is true for a clean end of file and false for a read or decoding failure. UTF-16LE/BE and UTF-32LE/BE are supported with codepages 1200/1201 and 12000/12001 respectively.
Pass codepage 0 to use automatic charset detection, matching {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}.
Reading is synchronous. For long-running processing, use the reader from a {@link Worker} to avoid blocking the panel UI.
Ordinary read and decoding failures are reported through {@link TextReader#ReadLine ReadLine} and {@link TextReader#EOF EOF}; they are not thrown as exceptions. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}.

params.name: codepage
params.description: Windows codepage used to decode each line. UTF-16LE/BE use 1200/1201, UTF-32LE/BE use 12000/12001, and 0 enables automatic detection. See Codepages.js.

returns.description: Open streaming reader, or null if the reader could not be created. This includes invalid or unsupported codepages, an empty filename, and ordinary file open failures.

name: ReadTextFile
description:
Performance note: supply codepage argument if it is known, since codepage detection might take some time.
UTF-8, UTF-16LE/BE, UTF-32LE/BE, and supported Windows codepages use the same decoding rules as {@link utils.OpenTextReader OpenTextReader}. A matching BOM is removed for UTF encodings.
For large line-oriented files, consider {@link utils.OpenTextReader OpenTextReader}; it avoids creating one JavaScript string containing the entire file.
Filesystem path resolution: absolute paths are used as-is. Relative paths are resolved against the file containing the current call. For the main script this is the main script directory; for an included script or a file-backed Worker it is that script's own directory. If there is no file-backed caller, the existing host fallback is used (the Worker's relative-path root, or the component directory for an in-memory panel script).

params.name: codepage
params.description: See Codepages.js. UTF-16LE/BE use 1200/1201, UTF-32LE/BE use 12000/12001. If codepage is 0, automatic detection is performed.

returns.description: Decoded file contents, or an empty string if the file could not be read or decoded.

examples: let text = utils.ReadTextFile("E:\\some text file.txt");

name: Run
signature: Run(target, args, working_dir, verb, show, wait)
description:
Runs a file, executable, URL, or document through the Windows shell.
This method uses ShellExecuteEx, so it supports shell verbs, file associations, URLs, and elevation through "runas".
Unlike {@link utils.RunCmdAsync RunCmdAsync}, this method does not capture stdout or stderr and does not provide timeout handling.
If wait is true, the call blocks until the launched process exits, when a process handle is available.
Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}. This applies only to working_dir; target is not path-resolved.

params.name: target
params.description:
File, executable, URL, or document to run/open.
If this value is empty, the method returns a {@link RunResult RunResult} with OK=false and Win32Error=ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.

params.name: args
params.description:
Command line arguments.
If a string is passed, it is appended as-is.
If an array is passed, each item is quoted automatically when needed.
For documents, URLs, or shell verbs that do not use parameters, this can be omitted.
For complex cmd.exe commands using shell syntax such as redirection, pipes, &, or &&, a string is usually more appropriate.

params.name: working_dir
params.description:
Working directory for the process.
Pass an empty string to use the default working directory.

params.name: verb
params.description:
Shell verb to use.
Pass an empty string to use the default verb.
Common values are "open", "edit", "print", and "runas".
Use "runas" to request elevation through UAC.

params.name: show
params.description:
Requested window display mode.
Use one of the {@link module:Flags.ShowWindow ShowWindow} values, for example {@link ShowWindow.Hide ShowWindow.Hide} or {@link ShowWindow.Show ShowWindow.Show}.
The target application or shell handler may ignore this value.

params.name: wait
params.description:
Whether to wait for the launched process to exit.
If false, OK means that ShellExecuteEx accepted the request.
If true, the method waits for the launched process to exit when a process handle is available, and then fills ExitCode.
When wait=true and a process exit code is available, OK is true only if the process exits with code 0.
A non-zero process exit code is reported as OK=false, with Win32Error usually remaining 0.
If wait=true but no process handle is available, OK=false and Win32Error=ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE.
Be careful: wait=true blocks the current script until the process exits and has no timeout.
Use {@link utils.RunCmdAsync RunCmdAsync} if you need asynchronous completion, stdout/stderr capture, or timeout handling.

returns.description: Result object.

name: RunCmdAsync
description:
Runs an external process asynchronously.
Standard output and standard error are captured separately.
The method returns a task id immediately, and the result is delivered later to on_run_cmd_async_done.
Completion callbacks may arrive in a different order than the {@link utils.RunCmdAsync RunCmdAsync} calls were made.
Use the returned task id to match the result with the original {@link utils.RunCmdAsync RunCmdAsync} call.
If the process does not finish before timeout_ms, the whole process tree is terminated.
Pass 0 as timeout_ms to wait indefinitely.
Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}. This applies only to working_dir; app is not path-resolved.

params.name: app
params.description:
Full path or executable name to run.
If this value is empty, the callback receives success=false and stderr contains an error message.

params.name: args
params.description:
Command line arguments.
If a string is passed, it is appended to the command line as-is.
If an array is passed, each item is quoted automatically when needed.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description:
Maximum time to wait for the process, in milliseconds.
Pass 0 to wait indefinitely.
On timeout, the callback receives success=false, exit_code=0xFFFFFFFF, and stderr contains a timeout message.

returns.description: Task id of the asynchronous operation.

throws.description: If args is invalid, the panel host is not fully initialized, or the worker thread cannot be started.

name: SHA1
description: Calculates SHA1 for string

returns.description: SHA1 value for input in hex format string. If input string is empty returns "da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709"

name: SHA1FromFile
description:
Calculates SHA1 value for file content

returns.description: SHA1 value for input file content in hex format string. If it was an error while reading file returns empty string. If file is empty returns "da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709"

name: ShowHtmlDialog
description:
Displays an html dialog, rendered by IE engine.
Utilizes the latest non-Edge IE that you have on your system.
Dialog is modal (blocks input to the parent window while open).

Html code and JavaScript executed inside the dialog must be IE compatible (see {@link https://www.w3schools.com/js/js_versions.asp}).

options.data is exposed inside the html dialog through window.external.dialogArguments. The bridge supports the following values:
  • Basic types: number, string, boolean, null, undefined
  • Arrays: call window.external.dialogArguments.toArray() inside html to obtain a JavaScript array. Each element has the same type limitations as options.data.
  • Functions: callable from html as callbacks into panel JavaScript. A callback may have a maximum of 7 arguments, and each argument has the same type limitations as options.data.
  • Objects are not transferred directly. Serialize them with JSON.stringify() before passing them and restore them with JSON.parse() inside html.
JSplitter objects such as {@link FbMetadbHandle FbMetadbHandle}, {@link GdiBitmap GdiBitmap} and {@link D2DBitmap} cannot be passed through this bridge.

The following properties are available through window.external inside the html dialog:
  • dialogArguments - read-only value containing options.data
  • dialogWindow - read-only native window handle (HWND) of the html dialog, represented as a number.
    It can be passed as window_id to JSplitter modal dialog functions to make the html dialog their owner, e.g.
    {@link utils.ColourPicker ColourPicker}
    {@link utils.FontPicker FontPicker}
    {@link utils.InputBox InputBox}
    {@link utils.TextBox TextBox}
    {@link plman.ShowPlaylistLockUI}
    {@link utils.FilePicker FilePicker}
    {@link utils.FolderPicker FolderPicker}
    {@link utils.MessageBox MessageBox}
    {@link utils.ShowHtmlDialog ShowHtmlDialog}
    The handle is valid only while the html dialog exists.

params.name: window_id
params.description: native window handle (HWND) to use as the dialog owner; pass 0 to use the default foobar2000 window

params.name: code_or_path
params.description: Html code or file path. File path must begin with file:// prefix.

params.name: options.x
params.description: Window horizontal position relative to desktop

params.name: options.y
params.description: Window vertical position relative to desktop

params.name: options.center
params.description: If true and if options.x and options.y are not set, will center window relative to fb2k position.

params.name: options.context_menu
params.description: If true, will enable right-click context menu.

params.name: options.resizable
params.description: If true, will allow to resize the window.

params.name: options.selection
params.description: If true, will allow to select everything (label texts, buttons and etc).

params.name: options.data
params.description: Read-only data exposed through window.external.dialogArguments. For multiple values, pass an array and call .toArray() inside html. Has type limitations described above.

throws.description: If no valid owner window is supplied and the panel host is not fully initialized, or the dialog cannot be created.

examples:
<caption>Dialog from file</caption>
utils.ShowHtmlDialog(0, `file://${fb.ComponentPath}samples/basic/html/PopupWithCheckBox.html`);

name: SplitFilePath

returns.description: An array of [directory, filename, filename_extension]

name: WriteBinaryFile
description:
Write raw binary data to a file.
For large output, consider {@link utils.OpenBinaryWriter OpenBinaryWriter}; it writes incrementally from a reusable caller-provided buffer. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}.

returns.description: true on success

throws.description: If data is not a Uint8Array.

name: WriteINI
description: Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}.
examples: utils.WriteINI("e:\\my_file.ini", "Last.fm", "username", "Bob");

name: OpenTextWriter
description:
Opens a text file for incremental writing.
The file is created or truncated when opened. The parent folder must already exist.
UTF-8 is used by default. UTF-16LE (1200), UTF-16BE (1201), UTF-32LE (12000), UTF-32BE (12001), and other valid Windows codepages are also supported.
If write_bom is true, the matching BOM is written for UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32. Other Windows codepages do not have a BOM and ignore this option.
Use {@link TextWriter#Write Write} to append text without a line terminator or {@link TextWriter#WriteLine WriteLine} to append text followed by CRLF. Encoding and I/O failures are reported through boolean return values. This avoids building one large JavaScript string before writing a large file.
Writing is synchronous. For one-shot large-file generation, use the writer inside {@link Worker.RunAsync}; for persistent pipelines, use it from a {@link Worker}. Both approaches keep blocking file I/O off the panel UI thread. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}.

params.name: write_bom
params.description: If true, writes a BOM for UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32.

params.name: codepage
params.description: Output Windows codepage. Codepage 0 is not valid for writing. See Codepages.js.

returns.description: Open streaming writer, or null if the writer could not be created. This includes an empty filename, an invalid codepage, and ordinary file creation/open failures.

name: WriteTextFile
description:
Note: the parent folder must already exist.
UTF-8 is used by default, matching {@link utils.OpenTextWriter OpenTextWriter}. UTF-16LE (1200), UTF-16BE (1201), UTF-32LE (12000), UTF-32BE (12001), and other valid Windows codepages are also supported.
If write_bom is true, the matching BOM is written for UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32. Other Windows codepages do not have a BOM and ignore this option.
For large output, consider {@link utils.OpenTextWriter OpenTextWriter}; it writes incrementally and does not require one large JavaScript string containing the entire file. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile ReadTextFile}.

params.name: codepage
params.description: Output Windows codepage. Codepage 0 is not valid for writing. See Codepages.js.

returns.description: true on success, false otherwise.

examples:
<caption>Default UTF-8 with BOM</caption>
utils.WriteTextFile("z:\\1.txt", "test");

<caption>UTF-8 without BOM</caption>
utils.WriteTextFile("z:\\2.txt", "test", false);

<caption>UTF-16LE with BOM</caption>
utils.WriteTextFile("z:\\3.txt", "test", true, 1200);

name: BinaryReader
description: Streaming binary reader returned by {@link utils.OpenBinaryReader}.

name: Read
description:
Reads bytes into an existing Uint8Array without allocating a new buffer.
If offset is omitted, reading starts at index 0. If count is omitted, bytes are read up to the end of the buffer.
An explicitly supplied offset + count must fit inside the buffer.

params.name: count
params.description: Maximum number of bytes to read. Defaults to the remaining buffer size.

returns.description: Number of bytes actually read. A nonzero request returning 0 means that no bytes were read: {@link BinaryReader#EOF EOF} is true at clean end of file and false if the read could not be performed. A zero-length request also returns 0.

throws.description: If the reader is closed.

name: Close
description: Closes the file. Calling {@link BinaryReader#Close Close} more than once is allowed.

returns.description: true if the reader is closed successfully; false if closing the file fails. Calling it again after a successful close returns true.

name: Length
description: File size in bytes as observed when the reader was opened.

name: Position
description: Number of bytes successfully read from the file.

name: EOF
description:
Indicates that the current read position has reached the file length recorded when the reader was opened.
This property does not report a closed reader or a read failure. Use the return value of {@link BinaryReader#Read Read} to drive the read loop; {@link BinaryReader#EOF EOF} is status information used to distinguish a clean end of file from a failed read.

name: Closed
description: Indicates whether the reader has been closed.

name: BinaryWriter
description: Streaming binary writer returned by {@link utils.OpenBinaryWriter}.

name: Write
description:
Writes bytes from an existing Uint8Array without creating a temporary typed array.
If offset is omitted, writing starts at index 0. If count is omitted, bytes are written up to the end of the buffer.
An explicitly supplied offset + count must fit inside the buffer.

params.name: count
params.description: Number of bytes to write. Defaults to the remaining buffer size.

returns.description: true on success; false if the buffer/range is invalid or the write fails.

throws.description: If the writer is closed.

name: Flush
description: Flushes buffered output to the file.

returns.description: true on success; false if flushing fails.

throws.description: If the writer is closed.

name: Close
description: Closes the file. Calling {@link BinaryWriter#Close Close} more than once is allowed.

returns.description: true if the writer is closed successfully; false if closing/flushing the file fails. Calling it again after a successful close returns true.

name: Position
description: Number of bytes successfully written to the file.

name: Closed
description: Indicates whether the writer has been closed.

name: SQLiteDatabase
description:
SQLite database returned by {@link utils.OpenDatabase}.
All operations are synchronous. Use a {@link Worker} for large imports, maintenance, or expensive queries when blocking the panel UI would be undesirable.
Parameter arrays are positional and must contain exactly as many values as the SQL statement requires. Booleans are stored as SQLite integers 0/1. Query results map SQLite NULL to null, INTEGER/REAL to number, TEXT to string, and BLOB to Uint8Array.
Database operations report SQL, binding, transaction-state, and closed-handle errors as JavaScript exceptions. {@link SQLiteDatabase#Close Close} is idempotent and does not throw.

name: Close
description:
Closes the database. Calling {@link SQLiteDatabase#Close Close} more than once is allowed.
This method does not throw; any SQLite close status is not exposed to script code.

returns.description: true after the database has been closed.

name: Begin
description: Starts a deferred transaction by executing BEGIN TRANSACTION.

throws.description: If a SQLite/database error occurs, including when the database is closed or the transaction cannot be started.

name: Commit
description: Commits the current transaction by executing COMMIT.

throws.description: If a SQLite/database error occurs, including when the database is closed or no transaction can be committed.

name: Rollback
description: Rolls back the current transaction by executing ROLLBACK.

throws.description: If a SQLite/database error occurs, including when the database is closed or no transaction can be rolled back.

name: Exec
description:
Executes one or more SQL statements. Result rows, if any, are discarded.
When multiple statements are supplied, parameter values are consumed in SQLite parameter-index order across the statements. The total parameter count must match exactly.

params.name: parameters
params.description: Positional parameter values. Supported element types: null, boolean, number, string, ArrayBuffer, and typed-array views.

throws.description: If an SQL, parameter, binding, or database error occurs, including an invalid parameter array/count or when the database is closed.

name: Query
description:
Executes exactly one SQL statement and returns all rows as plain JavaScript objects keyed by column name.
SQLite NULL becomes null, INTEGER/REAL become number, TEXT becomes string, and BLOB becomes Uint8Array. The query must produce unique column names; use SQL aliases when selecting duplicate names.

params.name: parameters
params.description: Positional parameter values. Supported element types: null, boolean, number, string, ArrayBuffer, and typed-array views.

returns.description: Query rows. Returns an empty array when the query produces no rows.

throws.description: If an SQL, parameter, binding, result-conversion, or database error occurs; multiple SQL statements are supplied; result column names are duplicated; or the database is closed.

name: Prepare
description:
Prepares exactly one SQL statement for repeated execution.
The returned statement owns its native SQLite handle. It is finalized automatically when the JavaScript object is destroyed, so calling {@link SQLiteStatement#Close Close} is not required for normal use. Call {@link SQLiteStatement#Close Close} only when the native statement should be released immediately.

returns.description: Prepared statement.

throws.description: If the SQL cannot be prepared, the input does not contain exactly one SQL statement, or the database is closed.

name: IsOpen
description: Indicates whether the database is open.

name: SQLiteStatement
description:
Prepared SQLite statement returned by {@link SQLiteDatabase#Prepare Prepare}.
A prepared statement is usable immediately after {@link SQLiteDatabase#Prepare Prepare} succeeds. Its native SQLite handle is finalized automatically when the JavaScript object is destroyed, so explicit cleanup is not required for normal use. {@link SQLiteStatement#Close Close} is provided only for releasing the native statement immediately when it is no longer needed.
{@link SQLiteStatement#Run Run} and {@link SQLiteStatement#Query Query} automatically reset the statement and clear all parameter bindings before returning, including when execution throws, so the same active statement can be reused immediately with a new parameter array.
Statement operations report parameter, binding, execution, result-conversion, and closed-handle errors as JavaScript exceptions. {@link SQLiteStatement#Close Close} is idempotent and does not throw.

name: Close
description:
Finalizes the prepared statement immediately and releases its native SQLite handle. Calling {@link SQLiteStatement#Close Close} more than once is allowed.
Explicit cleanup is optional: the statement is finalized automatically when the JavaScript object is destroyed. Use {@link SQLiteStatement#Close Close} when early release is useful, for example when many prepared statements are created while other work continues.
This method does not throw; any SQLite finalize status is not exposed to script code.

returns.description: true after the statement has been closed.

name: Run
description: Executes the prepared statement and discards any result rows. The statement is reset and its bindings are cleared before returning.

params.name: parameters
params.description: Positional parameter values. The count must match the prepared statement exactly.

throws.description: If a parameter, binding, or execution error occurs, including an invalid parameter array/count or when the statement is closed.

name: Query
description: Executes the prepared statement and returns all result rows. The statement is reset and its bindings are cleared before returning.

params.name: parameters
params.description: Positional parameter values. The count must match the prepared statement exactly.

returns.description: Query rows as plain JavaScript objects.

throws.description: If a parameter, binding, execution, or result-conversion error occurs, including an invalid parameter array/count, duplicate result column names, or when the statement is closed.

name: Reset
description:
Explicitly resets the statement and clears its current parameter bindings.
This is normally unnecessary after {@link SQLiteStatement#Run Run} or {@link SQLiteStatement#Query Query}, because both methods do it automatically.

throws.description: If the statement is closed or SQLite fails to clear its parameter bindings.

name: IsOpen
description:
Indicates whether the prepared statement still owns an active native SQLite handle.
This is true immediately after {@link SQLiteDatabase#Prepare Prepare} succeeds and becomes false after {@link SQLiteStatement#Close Close} is called. Normally there is no need to check this property unless the statement is being closed explicitly.

name: TextReader
description: Streaming text reader returned by {@link utils.OpenTextReader}.

name: ReadLine
description: Reads the next line and removes its line terminator.

returns.description: The next decoded line, or null when no line can be returned. When null is returned, {@link TextReader#EOF EOF} is true for clean end of file and false for a read or decoding failure.

throws.description: If the reader is closed.

name: Close
description: Closes the file. Calling {@link TextReader#Close Close} more than once is allowed.

returns.description: true if the reader is closed successfully; false if closing the file fails. Calling it again after a successful close returns true.

name: EOF
description:
Indicates that a clean end of file has been observed while reading.
This property does not report a closed reader or a read/decoding failure. Do not use it as a pre-read loop condition; use the return value of {@link TextReader#ReadLine ReadLine} to drive the loop, then inspect {@link TextReader#EOF EOF} when {@link TextReader#ReadLine ReadLine} returns null.

name: Closed
description: Indicates whether the reader has been closed.

name: TextWriter
description: Streaming text writer returned by {@link utils.OpenTextWriter}.

name: Write
description: Writes text at the current file position without adding a line terminator.

returns.description: true on success; false if the text cannot be encoded in the selected codepage or the write fails.

throws.description: If the writer is closed.

name: WriteLine
description: Writes text followed by a CRLF line terminator.

returns.description: true on success; false if the text cannot be encoded in the selected codepage or the write fails.

throws.description: If the writer is closed.

name: Flush
description: Flushes buffered output to the file.

returns.description: true on success; false if flushing fails.

throws.description: If the writer is closed.

name: Close
description: Closes the file. Calling {@link TextWriter#Close Close} more than once is allowed.

returns.description: true if the writer is closed successfully; false if closing/flushing the file fails. Calling it again after a successful close returns true.

name: Closed
description: Indicates whether the writer has been closed.

name: DriveInfo
description:
Object returned by {@link utils.GetDriveInfo}.
Property names and semantics follow the Microsoft Scripting Runtime Drive object where applicable.

name: Path
description: Drive path, for example C:. For a mapped network drive this is still the mapped drive path.

name: RootFolder
description: Root folder path, for example C:\.

name: DriveLetter
description: Drive letter without the colon, or an empty string when the volume has no drive letter.

name: DriveType
description:
Drive type.
Values are compatible with Scripting.FileSystemObject:
0 - unknown, 1 - removable, 2 - fixed, 3 - network, 4 - CD-ROM, 5 - RAM disk.

name: IsReady
description: true if volume or space information can be queried.

name: VolumeName
description: Volume label, or an empty string if unavailable. Writable for ready volumes.

name: FileSystem
description: File system name, or an empty string if unavailable.

name: SerialNumber
description: Volume serial number, or 0 if unavailable.

name: ShareName
description: Share name for a network drive, or an empty string for a local drive or when unavailable.

name: TotalSize
description: Total size in bytes, or 0 if unavailable.

name: FreeSpace
description: Total free space in bytes, or 0 if unavailable.

name: AvailableSpace
description: Free space available to the current user in bytes, or 0 if unavailable.

name: window

name: DlgCode
description:
Indicates which keys should be processed by the panel.
See {@link https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/desktop/dlgbox/wm-getdlgcode} for more info.

returns.description: See {@link module:Flags Flags} for flags like {@link module:Flags.DLGC_WANTARROWS DLGC_WANTARROWS}

examples: window.DlgCode = DLGC_WANTALLKEYS;

name: DPI
description: Window DPI. This value never changes while foobar2000 is running. If you change DPI settings, you must restart the application.

name: EraseOnRepaint
description:
Set whether the JSplitter panel should be cleared with background color before raising {@link module:Callbacks.on_paint on_paint} callback.
Default value: true.

name: DrawMode
description:
Current graphics rendering mode.
0 (default) - GDI+
1 - Direct2D
IMPORTANT: After switching the rendering mode, all drawing objects created for the other mode will be unavailable for use in the current mode.
Therefore, the developer should create all drawing objects only after changing the mode.
Ideally, the mode change should be made in the VERY first line of the main script to avoid accidentally creating objects of the wrong type.
Also, calling any of d2d.* methods for creating objects like fonts, bitmaps or effects, will cause a script crash until the {@link window.DrawMode DrawMode} is set to 1 at least once (in this case, the resources required for D2D operation are initialized). D2D rendering may differ from GDI and methods for both backends can not be expected to be 100% pixel equivalent.

name: ID
description: Window handle

name: InstanceType
description:
You need this to determine which GetFontXXX and GetColourXXX methods to use, assuming you want to support both interfaces.
See {@link module:Flags.UIInstanceType UIInstanceType}
0 - if using Columns UI
1 - if using default UI.

name: IsToolbar
description:
Indicates whether this JSplitter panel is hosted as a toolbar item in Columns UI.
This property is only meaningful when using Columns UI: it is true for a toolbar panel and false for a regular panel. It is always false in Default User Interface.

name: IsFocused
description:
Indicates whether this JSplitter panel currently has keyboard focus.
This reflects the same focus state reported by {@link on_focus}: it is true only while the panel window itself owns keyboard focus.

name: IsTransparent
description:
Only useful within Panel Stack Splitter (Columns UI component)
Depends on setting inside Spider Monkey Panel Configuration window. You generally use it to determine whether or not to draw a background.

name: JsMemoryStats
description:
SpiderMonkey heap and native/external memory statistics.
See {@link JsMemoryStats} for the returned object properties.

name: HostWindowTitle
description: Returns the title of the nearest named container hosting the panel.

name: MaxHeight
description:
{@link window.MaxHeight MaxHeight}, {@link window.MaxWidth MaxWidth}, {@link window.MinHeight MinHeight} and {@link window.MinWidth MinWidth} can be used to lock the panel size.
Do not use if panels are contained within Panel Stack Splitter (Columns UI component) or JSplitter itself

name: MaxWidth
description: See {@link window.MaxHeight MaxHeight}.

name: MinHeight
description: See {@link window.MaxHeight MaxHeight}.

name: MinWidth

name: Name

name: ScriptInfo
description: Information about the panel's main script. The {@link ScriptInfo.Path Path} property contains its full native filesystem path, or an empty string for an in-memory script. See {@link ScriptInfo} for all properties and source types.

name: Tooltip

params.name: reload_panel

name: ClearTimeout

name: ClearInterval

name: DefinePanel

Setups panel and script information and available features.
Can be called only once, so it's better to define it directly in the panel Configure menu.

params.name: options.features.grab_focus
params.description: Indicates if panel should grab mouse focus

throws.description: If called for a package script, called more than once, or options / options.features is not an object.

name: GetProperties
description: Get all current panel properties set by {@link window.SetProperty SetProperty}, {@link window.SetProperties SetProperties} or {@link window.ImportProperties ImportProperties}

returns.description: Map of panel properties

examples:
const props = window.GetProperties();
for(const [key, value] of props) console.log(`Key = ${key}, Value = ${value}`);

name: GetProperty
description:
Get value of property.
If property does not exist and default_val is not undefined and not null, it will be created with the value of default_val.

Note: leading and trailing whitespace are removed from property name.

name: ImportProperties
description:
Imports panel properties from file and (optionally) reloads the panel script
DOES clear all existing panel properties. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile}.

returns.description: If false, then an error occurred during import. Also, if an error occurs during import, the panel does not reload.

name: NotifyOthers
description:
This will synchronously trigger {@link module:Callbacks.on_notify_data on_notify_data}(name, info) in other panels.
!!! Beware !!!: data passed via info argument must NOT be used or modified in the source panel after invoking this method.
Legacy compatibility API
Existing scripts can keep using {@link window.NotifyOthers NotifyOthers} unchanged. For new asynchronous structured-clone messaging between panels and Workers, prefer {@link BroadcastChannel}.

name: Reload
description: Reloads panel.

params.name: clear_properties
params.description: If true, all panel properties will be cleared before reload

name: Repaint
description:
Performance note: don't force the repaint unless it's really necessary -
repaint calls might be grouped up when *not forced* which will turn them into a single repaint call,
thus reducing the amount of {@link module:Callbacks.on_paint on_paint} calls.

params.name: force
params.description: If true, will repaint immediately, otherwise a repaint task will be *scheduled*.

name: RepaintRect
description:
Repaints a part of the screen.
Use this instead of {@link window.Repaint Repaint} on frequently updated areas such as time, bitrate, seekbar, etc.

Performance note: see Performance note in {@link window.Repaint Repaint}.

params.name: force
params.description: If true, will repaint immediately, otherwise a repaint task will be *scheduled*.

name: SetCursor
description:
This would usually be used inside the {@link module:Callbacks.on_mouse_move on_mouse_move} callback.
Use -1 if you want to hide the cursor.

params.name: id
params.description: See {@link module:Flags Flags} for flags like {@link module:Flags.IDC_ARROW IDC_ARROW}

name: SetImePosition
description:
Sets the text insertion point used to position system IME UI for a custom-drawn text field. Coordinates are in panel client pixels. The component does not track or move the insertion point automatically; call this again whenever your script moves its caret.

This method does not create or draw a system caret. It only supplies the current insertion position to the IME so handwriting/candidate UI can be placed near the field.

name: SetInterval
description: See {@link setInterval}.

throws.description: If func is not callable or delay is zero.

name: SetProperties
description:
Set panel properties from input map and (optionally) reloads the panel script
Does NOT clear existing properties before setting.

params.name: reload_panel
params.description: If true, reloads panel script after setting

examples:
const values = new Map([["First value", 1], ["Second value", 2], ["Third value", 3]]);
window.SetProperties(values);

name: SetProperty
description:
Set property value.
Property will be removed, if val is undefined or null.

Property values are saved per panel instance and are remembered between foobar2000 restarts.

Note: leading and trailing whitespace are removed from property name.

name: SetShortcutFilter
description: Sets panel shortcut filter.

params.name: enabled
params.description: If true filter is enabled. Suppresses player shortcuts depending on the following two parameters

params.name: type_only
params.description: If true suppresses only shortcuts that identified as user input (keyboard_shortcut_manager::is_typing_message from SDK used). If false ALL shortcuts are disabled for panel

params.name: suppress_children
params.description: If true suppresses also shortcuts for all JSplitter's children. Takes into account the parameter type_only only for DUI. For CUI alwas disables ALL shortcuts

name: SetTimeout

throws.description: If func is not callable.

Show configuration window of current panel.

name: GetPanel

By default, it has the value of the panel plugin name, but it can be changed either directly in the window title (Show coords -> Click in caption text) or in the Columns UI placer (Use custom title) or in 'Panel list' (right click on JSplitter window)

throws.description: If no child panel exists with the specified name.

name: GetPanelCount
description: Get child panels count in JSplitter

name: GetPanelByIndex
description: Get an object for accessing the panel by index. the order depends on the position in the window stack: the bottommost window will have index 0.

throws.description: If no child panel exists at index.

name: CreateButton
description:
Creates a button in the splitter. 
The button will be created in the root of the window and will be placed at the coordinates (x, y). 
The function is also passed images to set the appearance of the button. 
The number of states the button can take will depend on the number of images passed to the function. 
hover_images - button images displayed when the mouse cursor hovers over the button. 
The function is flexible enough to create different types of buttons

name: GetButton
description: Get a button by its {@link ButtonObject#ID ID}

name: RadioButtons
description:
Creates a group of radio buttons. Takes an array of buttons as an argument. 
Each button must have at least two states, otherwise the function will fail.

throws.description: If buttons contains an invalid button object.

name: RemoveButton
description: Removes a button

name: MoveFoobarWindow
description: Deprecated compatibility API. It will be removed in a future release. Use {@link FbWindow#Move fb.Window.Move} for new code.

name: HandOnButtons
description:
Switches the mouse cursor for all buttons either to the hand or to the arrow. 
This property also affects all subsequently created buttons. 
This property can be changed individually for each button (see {@link ButtonObject} class).

name: TrackMouseEnterLeaveOnPanels
description:
Enables tracking of the mouse cursor entering/exiting the panel area. By default = false.
The following functions are used to handle events:
{@link module:Callbacks.on_panel_mouse_enter on_panel_mouse_enter}(name) - cursor entering the panel area, name is the panel name
{@link module:Callbacks.on_panel_mouse_leave on_panel_mouse_leave}(name) - cursor leaving the panel area, name is the panel name

name: TrackMouseMoveOnPanels
description:
Enables tracking of the mouse cursor position within the panel area.
By default = false . The following function is used to handle the event:
{@link module:Callbacks.on_panel_mouse_move on_panel_mouse_move}(name, x, y, mask): the event of moving the cursor within the panel area, name is the name of the panel, x, y are the coordinates of the point on the panel.

The destination must have room for at least SampleCount * ChannelCount values. This is useful for real-time visualizations that reuse the same buffer on every update; the legacy {@link FbAudioChunk#Data Data} property remains unchanged for compatibility.

name: AttachImage
description:
Embeds covers of the specified type, loaded from the specified file, into media files
Any existing artwork of the specified type will be overwritten!
Embedding covers is an asynchronous operation, so its result is not controlled here in any way. However, all the work of the method up to this point (reading file, creating art data) will return false in case of an error. Relative filesystem paths are resolved as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile}. URLs and foobar2000 URI paths are passed through unchanged.

returns.description: Returns false if any error occurred before the embedding started, otherwise true

name: AttachImage2
description:
Embeds covers of the specified type from exisiting {@link GdiBitmap GdiBitmap} or {@link D2DBitmap D2DBitmap} object. Supports JPEG, WEBP and PNG codecs for encoding image before embedding.
Any existing artwork of the specified type will be overwritten!
Embedding covers is an asynchronous operation, so its result is not controlled here in any way. However, all the work of the method up to this point (encoding, creating art data) will return false in case of an error.

params.name: image
params.description: (or {@link D2DBitmap} if {@link window.DrawMode} == 1). Image to attach

params.name: quality
params.description: NOTE: For WebP quality 100 means lossless WebP; values below 100 use lossy WebP. For PNG quality is ignored because PNG codec is always lossless.

returns.description: Returns false if any error occurred before the embedding started, otherwise true

name: FbUiSelectionHolder
description:
This is typically used to update the selection used by the default UI artwork panel
or any other panel that makes use of the preferences under
File > Preferences > Display > Selection viewers. Use in conjunction with the {@link module:Callbacks.on_focus on_focus}
callback.
examples:
<caption>For playlist viewers</caption>
let selection_holder = fb.AcquireUiSelectionHolder();
selection_holder.SetPlaylistSelectionTracking();

function on_focus(is_focused) {
    if (is_focused) { // Updates the selection when panel regains focus
        selection_holder.SetPlaylistSelectionTracking();
    }
}

<caption>For library viewers</caption>
let selection_holder = fb.AcquireUiSelectionHolder();
let handle_list = null;

function on_mouse_lbtn_up(x, y) { // Presumably going to select something here...
   handle_list = ...;
   selection_holder.SetSelection(handle_list);
}

function on_focus(is_focused) {
   if (is_focused) { // Updates the selection when panel regains focus
       if (handle_list && handle_list.Count)
           selection_holder.SetSelection(handle_list);
   }
}

description:
Returns up to max_count representative colours found in the image.
This is a legacy colour extraction method. For colour frequency information and more advanced clustering, use {@link GdiBitmap#GetColourSchemeJSON GetColourSchemeJSON} or {@link GdiBitmap#GetColourSchemeJSONV2 GetColourSchemeJSONV2}.

params.name: max_count
params.description: maximum number of colours to return

name: GetColourSchemeJSON
description:
Extracts representative colours from the image using K-means clustering in the RGB colour space.
Returns a JSON array in string form so you need to use JSON.parse() on the result.
Each entry contains a colour and its relative frequency in the clustered image.
Uses a different method for calculating colours than {@link GdiBitmap#GetColourScheme GetColourScheme}.
Image is automatically resized during processing for performance reasons so there's no need to resize before calling the method.

params.name: max_count
params.description: maximum number of colours to return

name: GetColourSchemeJSONV2
description:
Extracts representative colours from the image using K-means++ clustering in the Oklab colour space.
Returns a JSON array in string form so you need to use JSON.parse() on the result.
Each entry contains a colour and its relative frequency in the clustered image.
K-means++ initialization improves the distribution of the initial cluster centres, while Oklab provides a perceptually more uniform distance metric than RGB.
The optional min_chroma parameter limits the initial cluster centre selection to pixels with at least the specified Oklab chroma. It does not filter pixels or colours from the clustering result.

params.name: max_count
params.description: maximum number of colours to return

params.name: min_chroma
params.description: minimum Oklab chroma for pixels used as initial cluster centres

name: GetThemeColourSchemeJSON
description:
Builds an image-derived UI colour scheme for styling interface surfaces, text and interaction states from the bitmap.

The image is analysed in OKLab using the same weighted K-means++ palette extraction as {@link GdiBitmap#GetColourSchemeJSONV2 GetColourSchemeJSONV2}.
The palette stage uses paletteSize centroids, after which colours are assigned to five semantic UI roles:
Background, Text, Playing background, Focus frame and Selection background.

The returned colours are unsigned 32-bit ARGB values.
Background and Text are opaque.
State colours may contain alpha and are intended to be composited over Background.
playingBackgroundColor contains the Playing accent RGB together with the recommended alpha for a background highlight.
The same RGB channels can also be used at full opacity for a solid Playing indicator.

* The algorithm favours a representative image colour family for Background, prefers light body text unless the selected surface requires dark text, and uses independent image colour families for interaction/state accents when suitable candidates are available.

Returns an empty object {} if a colour scheme cannot be generated.

params.name: paletteSize
params.description: Palette size. Number of K-means++ colour centroids used as the input palette.

returns.description: JSON object string. Contains backgroundColor, textColor, playingBackgroundColor, focusFrameColor and selectionBackgroundColor.

name: HtmlDocument
description:
Object returned by {@link utils.ParseHtml}

Lightweight DOM-like HTML document backed by the native HTML parser.

Notes:
- This is not a full browser DOM.
- Scripts, CSS, layout, external resources and browser events are not processed.
- {@link HtmlDocument#innerText innerText} is currently an alias of {@link HtmlDocument#textContent textContent}.

description:

if (doc) console.log(doc.root.tagName); // "html"

description: Root document element, usually the <html> element.

if (doc) console.log(doc.documentElement.tagName); // "html"

description: The document <head> element.

if (doc && doc.head) console.log(doc.head.innerHTML); // "<title>Test</title>"

name: body
description: The document <body> element.
examples:
let doc = utils.ParseHtml("

Hello

"); if (doc && doc.body) console.log(doc.body.innerHTML); // "

Hello

"

name: textContent
description:
Text content of the document body.
If the document has no body, this falls back to the root element text.
Whitespace is returned as it exists in the parsed text nodes.

let doc = utils.ParseHtml("

Hello world

"); if (doc) console.log(doc.textContent); // "Hello world"

name: innerText
description:
Alias of {@link HtmlDocument#textContent textContent}.
Since this parser has no browser layout engine, {@link HtmlDocument#innerText innerText} does not emulate CSS visibility, rendered line wrapping, or layout-dependent text extraction.

Serialized HTML markup inside the document body.
If the document has no body, this falls back to the root element.
examples:
let doc = utils.ParseHtml("

Hello world

"); if (doc) console.log(doc.innerHTML); // "

Hello world

"

Hello

Hello

"

NOTE: {@link HtmlNode HtmlNode} objects keep the underlying native document alive while they exist.
