description:
Alias of {@link HtmlNode#textContent textContent}.
Since this parser has no browser layout engine, {@link HtmlNode#innerText innerText} does not emulate CSS visibility, rendered line wrapping, or layout-dependent text extraction.

name: innerHTML
description: Serialized HTML markup inside this node.

name: outerHTML
description: Serialized HTML markup of this node itself.

name: firstChild
description:
First child node.
Important: this can be a text node or comment, not necessarily an element.
Whitespace-only text nodes are preserved. Use JSON.stringify(node.textContent) while debugging if you need to see line breaks, tabs, and spaces explicitly. Use {@link HtmlNode#children children}[0] or {@link HtmlNode#querySelector querySelector} when you need an element.

name: childNodes
description: All child nodes, including element nodes, text nodes and comments.

name: children
description:
Child element nodes only.
Text nodes and comments are skipped.

name: getAttribute
description:
Returns an attribute value.
For missing attributes or non-element nodes, returns an empty string.

returns.description: Attribute value, or empty string.

name: hasAttribute
description:
Checks whether an element has an attribute.
For non-element nodes, returns false.

name: hasClass
description:
Checks whether the element has a CSS class token.
This checks class tokens, not arbitrary substrings.
For example, passing "album" to {@link HtmlNode#hasClass hasClass} matches class="album featured", but not class="album-list".
For non-element nodes, returns false.

name: querySelector
description: Returns the first descendant element matching a CSS selector.

returns.description: First matching node, or null if nothing matches.

name: querySelectorAll
description:
Returns all descendant elements matching a CSS selector.
The returned value is a regular JavaScript array.

returns.description: Array of matching nodes. Empty array if nothing matches.

name: getElementsByTagName
description:
Returns all descendant elements with the specified tag name.
Use "*" to return all descendant elements.

returns.description: Array of matching nodes. Empty array if nothing matches.

name: PanelObject
description: Panel object returned by {@link window.GetPanel} or {@link window.GetPanelByIndex}

name: Move
signature: Move(x, y, width, height, repaintParent = false)

name: ButtonObject
description: Button object returned by {@link window.CreateButton}

name: Click
description: Assigns click handler function. See also global callback 'on_button_click'

name: PerformanceEntry
description: Performance timeline entry created by {@link performance.mark performance.mark} or {@link performance.measure performance.measure}.

properties.name: entryType
properties.description: Entry type. JSplitter currently supports "mark" and "measure".

properties.name: name
properties.description: User-defined entry name.

properties.name: startTime
properties.description: Start timestamp in milliseconds relative to {@link performance.timeOrigin}.

properties.name: duration
properties.description: Entry duration in milliseconds. Always 0 for marks; for measures it is endTime - startTime and may be negative.

properties.name: detail
properties.description:
Optional metadata associated with the entry. Defaults to null.
JSplitter note: unlike the Web User Timing specification, {@link PerformanceEntry.detail detail} is currently retained as the original JavaScript value and is not structured-cloned.

name: PerformanceMarkOptions
description: Options accepted by {@link performance.mark performance.mark}.

properties.name: detail
properties.description:
Arbitrary metadata associated with the mark.
JSplitter note: the value is not structured-cloned.

properties.name: startTime
properties.description: Finite non-negative timestamp in milliseconds relative to {@link performance.timeOrigin}. Defaults to {@link performance.now performance.now}.

name: PerformanceMeasureOptions
description: Options accepted by the standard options form of {@link performance.measure performance.measure}.

properties.name: detail
properties.description:
Arbitrary metadata associated with the measure.
JSplitter note: the value is not structured-cloned.

properties.name: start
properties.description: Start mark name or finite non-negative timestamp in milliseconds.

properties.name: duration
properties.description: Finite non-negative duration in milliseconds. May be used together with {@link PerformanceMeasureOptions.start start} or {@link PerformanceMeasureOptions.end end}, but not together with both.

properties.name: end
properties.description: End mark name or finite non-negative timestamp in milliseconds.

name: PerformanceObserverOptions
description: Options accepted by {@link PerformanceObserver#observe PerformanceObserver.observe}.

properties.name: entryTypes
properties.description: Entry types to observe. Unsupported types are ignored. Use either {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.entryTypes entryTypes} or {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.type type} for an observer, not both.

properties.name: type
properties.description: A single entry type to observe. Unsupported types are ignored. Use either {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.type type} or {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.entryTypes entryTypes} for an observer, not both.

name: PerformanceObserverCallback
description: Callback invoked when observed performance entries are delivered.

name: PerformanceObserverEntryList
description:
List of performance entries delivered to a {@link PerformanceObserver PerformanceObserver} callback.
The entries in this list are ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntries
description: Returns all entries in this callback's entry list, ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntriesByType
description: Returns entries in this callback's entry list filtered by entry type and ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntriesByName
description: Returns entries in this callback's entry list filtered by name and, optionally, entry type. Results are ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

params.name: type
params.description: Optional entry type, for example "mark" or "measure".

name: PerformanceObserver
description:
Creates a new observer for entries added to the JSplitter performance timeline.
The callback is invoked asynchronously when {@link performance.mark performance.mark} or {@link performance.measure performance.measure} records an entry whose type is currently observed. Entries created in the same event-loop burst may be delivered together in one callback.
JSplitter currently supports only the "mark" and "measure" entry types. The Web Performance Timeline buffered option is not implemented.

params.name: callback
params.description: Callback invoked when matching entries are delivered.

name: supportedEntryTypes
description:
JSplitter compatibility alias for the standard static {@link PerformanceObserver PerformanceObserver.supportedEntryTypes} property.
Returns the same frozen array object as the static property.

name: observe
description:
Registers performance entry types to observe.
Use either {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.entryTypes entryTypes} or {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.type type} for a given observer until {@link PerformanceObserver#disconnect disconnect} is called. Switching between the two modes throws an error.
Repeated calls using the same mode add supported types to the observer's current set. Unsupported entry types are ignored.
JSplitter currently supports only {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.entryTypes entryTypes} and {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.type type}; the Web Performance Timeline buffered option is not implemented.

throws.description: If options is not an object or if the observer switches between {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.entryTypes entryTypes} and {@link PerformanceObserverOptions.type type} modes without first calling {@link PerformanceObserver#disconnect disconnect}.

name: disconnect
description:
Stops delivery of future performance entries, clears pending observer records, and resets the observer's registered entry types.
The same observer may be configured again with {@link PerformanceObserver#observe observe} after disconnecting.

name: takeRecords
description:
Returns the performance entries currently waiting in the observer buffer and empties that buffer.
Entries returned by this method will not later be delivered by the callback.

name: unknown@168
description:
Frozen array of entry types supported by {@link PerformanceObserver PerformanceObserver}.
JSplitter currently returns ["mark", "measure"]. Repeated reads return the same frozen array object.

name: performance
description:
High-resolution timing API implementing the JSplitter subset of the Web High Resolution Time, User Timing, and Performance Timeline APIs.
JSplitter currently records only user-created "mark" and "measure" entries; browser-specific navigation, resource, paint, and similar performance entry types are not available.
For the corresponding Web standards, see {@link https://www.w3.org/TR/hr-time-2/ High Resolution Time}, {@link https://www.w3.org/TR/user-timing/ User Timing}, and {@link https://www.w3.org/TR/performance-timeline/ Performance Timeline}.

name: now
description:
Returns a monotonically increasing high-resolution timestamp in milliseconds relative to {@link performance.timeOrigin timeOrigin}. The value may contain a fractional part; actual resolution depends on the underlying system clock.
Unlike Date.now(), this timestamp is intended for measuring elapsed time and is not affected by wall-clock adjustments.

name: mark
description:
Creates a named {@link PerformanceEntry} with {@link PerformanceEntry.entryType entryType} "mark" and adds it to the performance timeline.
Multiple marks may use the same name. All marks remain in the timeline until cleared; when a mark name is later used by {@link performance.measure measure}, the most recently created matching mark is used.

returns.description: The created mark entry.

throws.description: If startTime is not a finite non-negative number.

name: measure
description:
Creates a named {@link PerformanceEntry} with {@link PerformanceEntry.entryType entryType} "measure" and adds it to the performance timeline.
Standard forms of {@link performance.measure measure} supported by JSplitter: ```js performance.measure(name); // Timestamp 0 to performance.now(). performance.measure(name, startMark); // Most recent start mark to now. performance.measure(name, startMark, endMark); // Between the named marks. performance.measure(name, options); // Explicit start/end/duration options. performance.measure(name, {}, endMark); // Timestamp 0 to the named end mark. ``` See {@link PerformanceMeasureOptions} for the options object. In options, start and end may be either mark names or finite non-negative timestamps. duration may be supplied with exactly one of start or end. If an explicitly named mark does not exist, an error is thrown.
Multiple measures may use the same name. Named mark lookup always uses the most recently created matching mark.
Compatibility note: for historical JSplitter compatibility, a fourth legacyMeasureOptions argument is also accepted. This form preserves the previous JSplitter precedence rules: existing explicit startMark/endMark values take precedence, while numeric start, end, or duration options fill missing values. New code should prefer the standard forms above.
For backward compatibility, an empty positional mark name ("") is treated as omitted rather than as a mark named with an empty string.

params.name: startOrMeasureOptions
params.description: Start mark name or standard measure options.

params.name: legacyMeasureOptions
params.description: JSplitter legacy four-argument options object. Supports numeric start, end, duration, and arbitrary detail.

returns.description: The created measure entry.

throws.description: If a named mark cannot be resolved, a numeric timestamp/duration is invalid, or the standard options contain an invalid combination.

name: getEntries
description: Returns all {@link PerformanceEntry} objects currently stored in the performance timeline, ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntriesByType
description: Returns timeline entries filtered by entry type and ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntriesByName
description: Returns timeline entries filtered by name and, optionally, entry type. Results are ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

params.name: type
params.description: Optional entry type, for example "mark" or "measure".

name: clearMarks
description:
Removes mark entries from the performance timeline.
If name is supplied, all marks with that name are removed. If omitted, all mark entries are removed. Clearing a mark also removes it from subsequent named-mark lookup by {@link performance.measure measure}.

name: clearMeasures
description:
Removes measure entries from the performance timeline.
If name is supplied, all measures with that name are removed. If omitted, all measure entries are removed.

name: toString
description: JSplitter extension that returns a human-readable dump of the current performance timeline.

name: Observer
description:
JSplitter compatibility factory that creates a {@link PerformanceObserver PerformanceObserver}.
New code may use the standard {@link PerformanceObserver} constructor with a callback argument instead.

params.name: callback
params.description: Callback invoked when matching entries are delivered.

name: timeOrigin
description:
Read-only Unix timestamp in milliseconds corresponding to the origin used by this performance timeline.
{@link performance.now now} values are measured relative to this origin.

name: TitleFormatting
description:
JSplitter provides global Title Formatting fields for its statistics database and foobar2000 directories. These fields are available wherever foobar2000 evaluates global display fields, including formatting through {@link fb.TitleFormat} and {@link FbTitleFormat#EvalWithMetadb EvalWithMetadb}.

Statistics fields

These values belong to the JSplitter statistics database, not to audio-file tags. Scripts manage them through the linked {@link FbMetadbHandle} methods.
FieldValueSetter
%jsplitter_playcount%Play count stored by the script.{@link FbMetadbHandle#SetPlaycount SetPlaycount}
%jsplitter_loved%Loved value stored by the script.{@link FbMetadbHandle#SetLoved SetLoved}
%jsplitter_first_played%First-played string stored by the script.{@link FbMetadbHandle#SetFirstPlayed SetFirstPlayed}
%jsplitter_last_played%Last-played string stored by the script.{@link FbMetadbHandle#SetLastPlayed SetLastPlayed}
%jsplitter_rating%Rating value stored by the script.{@link FbMetadbHandle#SetRating SetRating}
Numeric fields are absent when their stored value is 0; string fields are absent when empty. {@link FbMetadbHandle#ClearStats ClearStats} clears all five values. No fixed rating scale or date-string format is imposed by these fields.

Directory fields

FieldValueJavaScript equivalent
%jsplitter_fb2k%foobar2000 installation directory.{@link fb.FoobarPath}
%jsplitter_fb2k_profile%foobar2000 profile/configuration directory.{@link fb.ProfilePath}
Both values are native filesystem paths and support Unicode. They are initialized at startup and remain fixed for the session. The fields use the jsplitter_ prefix so they do not register the unprefixed names used by other components.

Using fields in JavaScript

Evaluate Title Formatting through {@link fb.TitleFormat}; the field names are not JavaScript variables. {@link FbTitleFormat#Eval Eval} with true also evaluates the expression when playback is stopped: ```js const profile = fb.TitleFormat('%jsplitter_fb2k_profile%').Eval(true); const imagePath = profile + '\\images\\cover.png'; ``` Statistics fields refer to the track being formatted: ```js const track = fb.GetNowPlaying(); if (track) { const rating = fb.TitleFormat('$if2(%jsplitter_rating%,0)').EvalWithMetadb(track); console.log(rating); } ```

Process environment variables

The directory names jsplitter_fb2k and jsplitter_fb2k_profile are also set as Windows environment variables in the foobar2000 process. Their values are the same paths as the Title Formatting fields. Child processes inherit them when they inherit foobar2000's environment. The system-wide and user environment are not modified. A path input field can expand %jsplitter_fb2k% or %jsplitter_fb2k_profile% if its component supports the corresponding Title Formatting or environment-variable expansion. Registration does not make every text field perform expansion automatically.

Relative paths inside scripts

Supported file and image methods resolve relative paths as described in {@link utils.ReadTextFile}. To obtain the main script's own full path for custom path handling or external tools, use the {@link ScriptInfo.Path Path} property of {@link window.ScriptInfo}. Directory fields identify foobar2000 directories, not the main script's directory.

name: AudioChannelInfo
description: PCM channel entry contained in {@link AudioFormat}.

properties.name: Index
properties.description: Zero-based position of the channel in interleaved PCM samples. This value can be passed directly to visualization channel properties.

properties.name: Flag
properties.description: Speaker-position bit from {@link AudioFormat.ChannelConfig ChannelConfig}. Combining the flags of all channel entries produces the format's channel mask.

properties.name: Names
properties.description:
Known lower-case names for this speaker position. The first value is the canonical full name; subsequent values are short or familiar aliases. The array is empty for an unknown channel flag.
Canonical nameAliases
front-leftfl, left
front-rightfr, right
front-centerfc, center
low-frequency-effectslfe
back-leftbl, rear-left
back-rightbr, rear-right
front-center-leftfcl
front-center-rightfcr
back-centerbc, rear-center
side-leftsl
side-rightsr
top-centertc
top-front-lefttfl
top-front-centertfc
top-front-righttfr
top-back-lefttbl
top-back-centertbc
top-back-righttbr

name: AudioFormat
description:
Current visualization PCM-format snapshot returned by {@link vis.AudioFormat}.
It describes the post-processing stream received by visualizations and can therefore differ from the source file's format.

properties.name: SampleRate
properties.description: PCM sample rate in hertz.

properties.name: ChannelCount
properties.description: Number of interleaved PCM channels.

properties.name: ChannelConfig
properties.description: foobar2000 channel-mask value describing the speaker positions in the stream.

properties.name: Channels
properties.description: Channel entries ordered by PCM index. The array contains {@link AudioFormat.ChannelCount ChannelCount} entries.

name: ShaderCacheStats
description:
Snapshot of the process-wide native HLSL-to-DXBC LRU cache returned by
{@link vis.ShaderCacheStats}. Counts cover automatic HLSL compilation performed
by {@link vis.CreateAsync}; {@link d2d.Compile}, {@link d2d.CompileAsync} and
supplied DXBC are excluded. {@link ShaderCacheStats.Hits Hits},
{@link ShaderCacheStats.Misses Misses} and {@link ShaderCacheStats.Evictions Evictions}
accumulate during the process lifetime.

properties.name: Entries
properties.description: Number of cached compiled HLSL programs.

properties.name: Bytes
properties.description: Approximate CPU bytes retained for source/profile strings and DXBC buffers; excludes GPU memory and container overhead.

properties.name: Hits
properties.description: Requests served by a cached HLSL compilation result.

properties.name: Misses
properties.description: Cache lookups that did not find the requested HLSL program; concurrent requests can both miss.

properties.name: Evictions
properties.description: Entries removed when limits are exceeded or reduced.

name: VisualizationShaderCode
description: Shader program accepted by {@link vis.CreateAsync} in any renderer stage. A string must contain non-empty HLSL with entry point main. Bytecode must be valid DXBC for ps_4_0, ps_4_1 or ps_5_0, in a non-empty, non-shared buffer that has not been detached. The GPU must support the chosen shader profile. Every program must follow the source or image-pass input layout described in {@link module:Visualizations Visualization API}.

name: VisualizationImagePass

properties.name: shader
properties.description: Program that processes the preceding RGBA image at t0 with sampler s0.

properties.name: textures
properties.description: One to three non-empty image-file paths, bound in order at t1–t3 with samplers s1–s3. Omit this property, or pass null, when no files are needed; an empty array is not accepted. Paths use the usual script image-path resolution. Files are loaded during asynchronous creation and retained as decoded image data. After a graphics-device reset, GPU textures are recreated from that data; files are not read again. To load changed file contents, create a new visualization. Each pass sees only its own images.

name: VisualizationShaderRenderer
description:
Renderer configuration for {@link vis.CreateAsync}. Source analysis settings
belong in the second argument. Shader output uses premultiplied RGBA.

properties.name: shader
properties.description: Required program that draws from the selected native audio source.

properties.name: feedback
properties.description: One image pass transforming previous history before the current source is composited over it. Omit or pass null to disable feedback.

properties.name: post
properties.description:
One image pass or an array of 1–4 passes, executed in order after the current image is complete.
   Each reads the preceding image. Omit or pass null to disable post-processing.

properties.name: feedbackIntervalMs
properties.description:
Feedback-history interval: 0 for every {@link Visualization#Draw Draw}, or a finite number from 1 to 1000 milliseconds.
   A positive value requires {@link VisualizationShaderRenderer.feedback feedback}. Change it later through {@link Visualization#FeedbackIntervalMs FeedbackIntervalMs}.
   This setting does not create a timer; missed intervals are skipped and post passes still run on each draw.

properties.name: feedbackTransparent
properties.description: Start and composite history over transparent black instead of opaque black, retaining shader alpha. A true value requires {@link VisualizationShaderRenderer.feedback feedback}.

properties.name: stopOnPause
properties.description:
Freeze the last completed image, including post effects, while playback is paused.
   A frozen image is scaled on resize without reprocessing. When false, shaders continue to run using retained audio data.
   This setting does not stop native audio analysis or schedule panel repaints.

name: vis
description:
Creates visualizations and manages the per-panel native audio analysis service.
For a guided introduction, see {@link module:Visualizations Visualization API}.

name: UpdateIntervalMs
description:
Native audio analysis update interval, in milliseconds.
Default: 16. Accepts unsigned integer milliseconds from 1 to 4,294,967,295. This changes the cadence of the shared audio engine, not the panel repaint interval or shader feedback cadence.

name: AudioFormat
ShaderTarget
description: HLSL compiler profile used by subsequent {@link vis.CreateAsync CreateAsync} calls in this panel. Default: "ps_4_0". Allowed: "ps_4_0", "ps_4_1", "ps_5_0". Each call captures the profile for all its HLSL stages. Changing it does not alter pending compilations, existing visualizations or supplied DXBC. The chosen profile must be supported by the GPU. This property does not change the defaults of {@link d2d.Compile} or {@link d2d.CompileAsync}.

name: ShaderFlags
description: HLSL compiler flags used by subsequent {@link vis.CreateAsync CreateAsync} calls in this panel. Default: 0x8008, combining optimization level 3 and row-major matrix packing. Accepts an unsigned 32-bit bitmask; see {@link module:Flags.D2DCompileFlags D2DCompileFlags}. The mask is forwarded unchanged to the compiler for every HLSL stage in the call. Like {@link vis.ShaderTarget ShaderTarget}, it is captured at creation time and does not affect supplied DXBC or the separate defaults of {@link d2d.Compile} and {@link d2d.CompileAsync}. Target and flags are part of the native shader-cache key.

name: ShaderCacheMaxEntries
description: Maximum number of HLSL-to-DXBC programs retained in the shared native LRU cache. Default: 128; allowed range: 0–4096. The limit applies across all JSplitter panels and takes effect immediately. Set to zero to disable this cache. Changing the value can evict entries, but does not interrupt shader visualizations that are already running. This setting is not persisted across foobar2000 restarts.

name: ShaderCacheMaxBytes
description: Approximate CPU-memory limit for retained HLSL source/profile strings and compiled DXBC in the shared native LRU cache, in bytes. Default: 16777216 (16 MiB); allowed range: 0–1073741824 (1 GiB). Both the byte limit and {@link vis.ShaderCacheMaxEntries ShaderCacheMaxEntries} must be satisfied; zero in either property disables caching. Changes take effect immediately and are not persisted across restarts. Does not include GPU memory.

name: ShaderCacheStats
description:
Snapshot of five statistics from the process-wide HLSL compilation cache. Each read creates a new object; the numbers are not live-updating properties. See {@link ShaderCacheStats} for its five fields. Read the limits separately via {@link vis.ShaderCacheMaxEntries ShaderCacheMaxEntries} and {@link vis.ShaderCacheMaxBytes ShaderCacheMaxBytes}. {@link d2d.Compile} and {@link d2d.CompileAsync} do not populate this cache; shader HLSL compiled by {@link vis.CreateAsync CreateAsync} does.

Example:

```js const s = vis.ShaderCacheStats; console.log(`${s.Entries}/${vis.ShaderCacheMaxEntries} shaders, ` + `${(s.Bytes / 1048576).toFixed(2)} MiB; ` + `${s.Hits} hits, ${s.Misses} misses, ${s.Evictions} evictions`); ```

name: Create
description:
Creates a visualization with a built-in renderer or JavaScript drawing callback synchronously.
source_id selects one of six native audio sources. Use a numeric source ID (0–5) or a named constant from {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType} after loading docs/Flags.js with {@link include}. Omitted, null or undefined source_params and renderer use the defaults. When a source snapshot is available, a callback receives (gr, x, y, width, height, data) when {@link Visualization#Draw Draw} is called; native analysis still prepares its data. See {@link module:Visualizations Visualization API} for source settings, built-in renderer settings and callback data. Use {@link vis.CreateAsync CreateAsync} for HLSL/DXBC renderers.

Example:

```js include('docs/Flags.js'); const waveform = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Waveform); const envelope = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Waveform, { points: 256 }, { style: "envelope" }); ```

params.name: source_id
params.description: Numeric audio source ID (0-5). See {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType}

params.name: source_params
params.description: Initial native source analysis settings or null.

params.name: renderer
params.description: Built-in display settings or JS drawing callback.

name: CreateAsync
description:
Creates a shader visualization and returns a Promise resolving to it. Requires a {@link VisualizationShaderRenderer}; built-in settings and JavaScript drawing callbacks use {@link vis.Create Create} instead.

HLSL stages are compiled off the UI thread using the current {@link vis.ShaderTarget ShaderTarget} and {@link vis.ShaderFlags ShaderFlags} and can be reused through the shared shader cache. Precompiled DXBC bypasses HLSL compilation. Configuration, compilation and creation failures reject the Promise.

Draw only after the Promise resolves, with {@link window.DrawMode} set to 1 (Direct2D). Creation does not schedule repaints. Source runtime properties remain available; shader programs and pipeline structure are fixed at creation time, while {@link Visualization#FeedbackIntervalMs FeedbackIntervalMs} remains adjustable.

Example:

```js include('docs/Flags.js'); window.DrawMode = 1; let visual = null; // 'hlsl' contains a complete source shader; see the linked examples. vis.CreateAsync(VisSourceType.Waveform, null, { shader: hlsl }) .then(v => { visual = v; window.Repaint(); }) .catch(e => console.log("Visualization creation failed: " + e)); ```

params.name: source_id
params.description: Numeric audio source ID (0–5). See {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType}

params.name: source_params
params.description: Initial native source analysis settings, or null/undefined to use defaults.

name: Visualization
description:
Visualization object returned by {@link vis.Create} and {@link vis.CreateAsync}. This is a documentation-only instance description, not a constructor exposed by the {@link vis} namespace. A visualization retains its native audio subscription while alive.
Source runtime properties are exposed directly on this object; built-in renderers add their renderer properties to the same object. Shader visualizations expose {@link Visualization#FeedbackIntervalMs FeedbackIntervalMs} and {@link Visualization#InjectFeedback InjectFeedback}. See {@link module:Visualizations Visualization API} for the complete property tables.

name: Draw
description:
Draws this visualization within the specified rectangle. Call from {@link module:Callbacks.on_paint on_paint} using the current graphics context. The method does not change {@link vis.UpdateIntervalMs} or schedule another repaint. With shader feedback enabled, it also advances history when a step is due.
Built-in and JavaScript callback renderers support GDI and Direct2D; shader renderers created with {@link vis.CreateAsync CreateAsync} require Direct2D.

name: InjectFeedback

params.name: bitmap
params.description: Direct2D bitmap with the image to add to history, normally on a transparent background.

throws.description: If feedback is absent, the bitmap is invalid, exceeds the feedback limits or uses an incompatible Direct2D device.

name: FeedbackIntervalMs
description:
Shader feedback interval in milliseconds. Use 0 to advance history on every
{@link Visualization#Draw Draw}, or a finite number from 1 to 1000 for a fixed
cadence; fractional values are supported. Positive values require a feedback
pass. Without feedback, the property reads 0 and accepts only 0.

Changing the value preserves history and other visualization state. The next
eligible {@link Visualization#Draw Draw} uses the new cadence; assigning the same
value leaves the current schedule intact. This property does not create a timer
or request a repaint, and missed history steps are skipped. See
{@link module:Visualizations Visualization API} for shader timing details.
```js
// visual already has a feedback pass; keep requesting panel repaints.
visual.FeedbackIntervalMs = 1000 / 120; // Fixed 120-Hz history step.
const interval = visual.FeedbackIntervalMs;
visual.FeedbackIntervalMs = 0;          // History advances on each Draw.
```

throws.description:
If the value is not a finite number equal to 0 or within
1..1000, or a positive value is assigned without a feedback pass.

name: SourceType
description: Numeric native source type used to create this visualization. See {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType}

name: RendererType
description: Renderer family: built-in, JavaScript callback, or shader. See {@link module:Flags.VisRendererType VisRendererType}

name: DebugInfo
description:
Diagnostic information about this visualization and its native audio
engine, including source and feedback statistics when applicable.

name: WebAssembly
description:
JSplitter exposes the standard {@link module:WebAssembly WebAssembly} global in both panels and {@link Worker Workers}. {@link module:WebAssembly WebAssembly} modules built from C, C++, Rust or other supported languages can run directly in SpiderMonkey without additional native support from JSplitter.

Loading a module

The simplest approach is to read a local .wasm file as bytes with {@link utils.ReadBinaryFile}, then create a module and an instance: ```js const bytes = utils.ReadBinaryFile('algorithm.wasm'); if (!bytes) throw new Error('Cannot read WASM module'); const module = new WebAssembly.Module(bytes); const instance = new WebAssembly.Instance(module); // Call instance.exports.someFunction(...) ``` For CPU-intensive tasks, consider running {@link module:WebAssembly WebAssembly} in a {@link Worker} to keep the panel responsive.

Ready-to-run example: album-art filters

The samples/wasm folder contains a practical example of Sobel edge detection, implemented in C and compiled to a standalone WASM module. It loads the playing or focused track's cover using {@link utils.GetAlbumArtV2}. When no artwork is available, it displays a generated test image instead. GDI shows the original and filtered artwork side by side. To run: select Script → File in a JSplitter panel and choose samples/wasm/WebAssembly Image Filters.js. Do not move this file separately from its Worker or WASM dependencies. The script is ready to run from the distributed samples directory; no build step or additional runtime is necessary. A panel of roughly 650 × 350 pixels works well.
  • Left click: switch between Pencil, Neon and Ink modes.
  • Mouse wheel: adjust edge-detection threshold.
  • Right click: refresh the selected or playing track's cover.

How the example works

  1. The panel obtains an image and extracts RGBA pixels using {@link GdiBitmap#GetPixelData GdiBitmap.GetPixelData}, then transfers their buffer to a file-backed {@link Worker} via {@link Worker#postMessage Worker.postMessage}.
  2. The Worker reads album_art_filters.wasm with {@link utils.ReadBinaryFile}, then constructs its WebAssembly.Module and WebAssembly.Instance once.
  3. The Worker copies image pixels into the module's exported WebAssembly.Memory. The native filter function reads that region and writes processed RGBA pixels into another region.
  4. The output is copied out of WASM memory and sent back to the panel, which creates an image via {@link gdi.CreateImageFromPixelData}.
  5. Changing the mode or threshold reuses the existing instance and source pixels in the Worker. Only small parameters need to be sent again.

Memory and data exchange

Compiled code uses offsets into linear WebAssembly.Memory, not direct pointers to arbitrary JavaScript objects. This example obtains the beginning of usable memory from the exported __heap_base global and reserves two aligned RGBA buffers. It grows the memory when required and recreates typed-array views after growth. To transfer the result back, it first copies the output into a separate JavaScript Uint8Array, leaving WASM memory owned by the Worker.

Included files

  • WebAssembly Image Filters.js — GDI panel and controls.
  • WebAssembly Image Filters.worker.js — Worker and WASM integration.
  • album_art_filters.wasm — ready-to-run standalone module.
  • source/album_art_filters.c — original C implementation.
  • README.md — optional Clang build command.

Limitations

{@link module:WebAssembly WebAssembly} is not automatically a browser or operating-system runtime. Modules built for WASI, Emscripten, Node.js, the DOM, network access, or multi-threading may require additional imports, JavaScript support, or APIs that JSplitter does not provide. {@link module:WebAssembly WebAssembly} also does not guarantee a performance improvement over JavaScript or native code. The timer displayed by this example includes the WASM function call and copying of its output buffer, not full end-to-end rendering or image loading. The example limits image dimensions to 384 pixels per side to bound memory and CPU cost, including on 32-bit foobar2000. Only use WASM modules whose behavior and resource requirements you trust.

Building the WASM module (optional)

The prebuilt album_art_filters.wasm is included and runs without a build step. To rebuild it after editing source/album_art_filters.c, install Clang with {@link module:WebAssembly WebAssembly} (wasm32) support and wasm-ld. Run the following from component/samples/wasm: ```sh clang --target=wasm32-unknown-unknown -O3 -nostdlib \ -Wl,--no-entry -Wl,--export=filter -Wl,--export-memory \ -Wl,--export=__heap_base -Wl,--initial-memory=131072 \ -o album_art_filters.wasm source/album_art_filters.c ``` On Windows, enter the command on a single line, removing the backslashes used for line continuation. The command writes album_art_filters.wasm next to the Worker script. The -nostdlib and --no-entry options avoid a C runtime entry point; the linker exports the filter function, linear memory and __heap_base needed by the Worker. This is a build-time step outside JSplitter. The panel and Worker simply load the already-built module.

name: RunAsync
description:
Runs a user-defined JavaScript callback once in a temporary Worker and returns a Promise for its result.
A fresh full Worker realm/thread is created for every call. Arguments are structured-cloned into the Worker; a synchronous return value or the resolved value of an asynchronous callback is structured-cloned back. The temporary Worker is terminated automatically when the operation settles.
The callback is recreated from its source and does not capture lexical variables from the caller. Pass required values explicitly through args. Native and bound functions are not supported. Relative {@link include} calls keep the caller's script/package roots.
This API does not currently expose a transfer list. For repeated requests, persistent Worker state, or explicit ownership transfer, use a normal {@link Worker} and {@link Worker#postMessage postMessage}.

params.name: callback
params.description: User-defined JavaScript function to execute in the temporary Worker. The function may return a value or a Promise.

params.name: args
params.description: Values passed to callback through structured clone.

returns.description: Promise resolved with the structured-cloned callback result. It rejects if the callback throws or rejects, the callback cannot be recreated, Worker startup fails, or an argument/result cannot be structured-cloned.

throws.description: If callback is not callable or the {@link Worker.RunAsync RunAsync} helper itself cannot be initialized.

name: onerror
description:
Receives uncaught Worker errors reported to the parent endpoint as an {@link ErrorEvent}.
The callback argument exposes the error text through {@link ErrorEvent#message message} and the original Worker source location through {@link ErrorEvent#filename filename}, {@link ErrorEvent#lineno lineno} and {@link ErrorEvent#colno colno}.
If no parent error handler exists, the Worker error is promoted to the normal panel-script error UI/failure path. Throwing from this handler likewise propagates as a normal panel script exception, whose stack begins in the parent handler.

name: Visualizations
description:
JSplitter provides a visualization API built around reusable audio sources and renderers. A source prepares audio measurements; a renderer turns them into a picture. Six native sources are available: Waveform, Spectrum, Peak Meter, VU Meter, Spectrogram, and Vectorscope. Each source can use its built-in renderer or provide data to a custom JavaScript or shader renderer.

This article covers both approaches: it starts with the built-in visualizations and their settings, then explains how the same sources can be used with custom renderers.

How the analysis engine works

Each panel has one native analysis engine shared by its visualizations. It starts with the first visualization, stops after the last one is released, and performs audio analysis on a dedicated thread.

Active sources request only the measurements they need, and compatible analysis work is reused automatically. {@link vis.UpdateIntervalMs} controls the requested analysis cadence; the default is 16 ms. Panel repainting is independent: scripts request repaints and {@link Visualization#Draw Draw} renders the latest available snapshot.

Creating your first visualization

Start playback and run this complete script in a panel. It creates one waveform, draws it in the paint callback and requests regular repaints:

```js include('docs/Flags.js'); // Create a waveform visualization with default settings and built-in renderer. const waveform = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Waveform); // Match the background as well, so theme-colored content remains visible. const backgroundColor = window.InstanceType === UIInstanceType.DefaultUI ? window.GetColourDUI(ColourTypeDUI.background) : window.GetColourCUI(ColourTypeCUI.background); function on_paint(gr) { const w = window.Width, h = window.Height; gr.FillSolidRect(0, 0, w, h, backgroundColor); if (w > 0 && h > 0) waveform.Draw(gr, 0, 0, w, h); } setInterval(() => window.Repaint(), 33); // Request roughly 30 FPS presentation. ```

{@link include include} loads the named constants used by the script. {@link module:Callbacks.on_paint on_paint} paints the panel, {@link Visualization#Draw Draw} draws the latest visualization snapshot inside the specified rectangle, and the timer requests another paint with {@link window.Repaint Repaint}. A visualization does not clear the panel, so draw the background before calling {@link Visualization#Draw Draw}. The built-in renderer uses the active UI text color by default; the example therefore uses the matching DUI/CUI background color.

Sources and renderers

Audio reaches the engine as PCM (Pulse-Code Modulation): successive amplitude samples for each channel.

{@link vis.Create vis.Create} creates a visualization from one of JSplitter's native audio sources.

```text Create(source_id[, source_params, renderer]) ```

source_id selects which audio source to use. It is a numeric source ID from 0 to 5; for readability, use the corresponding {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType} constants.

source_params configures the source analysis. Available settings depend on the selected source and are listed with each visualization below. Omit the argument, or pass null or undefined, to use the source defaults.

```js const spectrum = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Spectrum, { fftSize: 2048 }); ```

renderer controls how the source data is displayed. With {@link vis.Create Create}, pass either a built-in renderer settings object or a JavaScript drawing callback. Omit the argument, or pass null or undefined, to use the default built-in renderer.

```js const waveform = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Waveform, null, { style: "line", lineWidth: 2 }); ```

The returned {@link Visualization} object has {@link Visualization#Draw Draw}, which draws inside the specified rectangle in panel pixels. The visualization does not schedule repaints by itself, so the script requests them with {@link window.Repaint window.Repaint}. Create the visualization once, outside {@link module:Callbacks.on_paint on_paint}.

Built-in renderers support both GDI and Direct2D. They draw through the graphics context passed to {@link Visualization#Draw Draw}. JavaScript callback renderers likewise use the panel's current GDI or Direct2D context. Only shader renderers created with {@link vis.CreateAsync CreateAsync} require Direct2D ({@link window.DrawMode} = 1).

Changing settings at runtime

The returned {@link Visualization} object exposes settings that can be inspected and changed at runtime. The tables below pair creation settings with their corresponding runtime properties. Unless noted otherwise, exposed settings are readable and writable.

Source and renderer settings are exposed on the same visualization object. Source properties remain available with every renderer type. Built-in renderer properties are exposed only by built-in visualizations; JavaScript callbacks perform their own drawing, while shader visualizations expose only their shader-specific renderer properties.

```js const waveform = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Waveform, { points: 256 }, { style: "envelope" }); waveform.Points = 512; waveform.Style = "line"; ```

Creation settings use lower camel case, such as fftSize; the corresponding runtime properties use JSplitter property naming, such as FftSize. Changing a runtime property updates the running visualization.

On the returned visualization object, {@link Visualization#SourceType SourceType}, {@link Visualization#RendererType RendererType}, and {@link Visualization#DebugInfo DebugInfo} are read-only.

Selecting source channels

Waveform, Spectrum, Peak Meter, VU Meter, and Spectrogram use channel to select the audio input. Vectorscope uses leftChannel and rightChannel instead.

A channel selector accepts a channel name or PCM index:

```js const left = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Waveform, { channel: "left" }); const second = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Waveform, { channel: 1 }); ```

The same selector can be changed later through Channel:

```js left.Channel = "right"; ```
SelectorMeaning
"mix"Mix all available channels to mono. This is the default.
Channel nameSelect a speaker position such as "left", "right", or "rear-left".
Non-negative integerSelect a fixed PCM channel index.

To inspect the channels available in the current stream, use {@link vis.AudioFormat}. Its {@link AudioFormat.Channels Channels} array lists them in PCM index order with their known names:

```js const format = vis.AudioFormat; if (format) { for (const channel of format.Channels) { console.log(channel.Index, channel.Names); } } ```

{@link vis.AudioFormat} describes the current post-processing PCM stream, so it may differ from the source file after DSP, downmixing, or upmixing. It is null when no current audio format is available. See {@link AudioFormat} for the complete object.

Vectorscope uses two selectors instead: leftChannel and rightChannel at creation time, and LeftChannel and RightChannel at runtime. They accept channel names or PCM indices, but not "mix":

```js const vectorscope = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Vectorscope, { leftChannel: "left", rightChannel: "right" }); ```

Built-in visualizations

JSplitter provides a built-in renderer for each native visualization source. The sections below show creation examples, screenshots, and the corresponding source and renderer settings.

Interactive showcase: Builtin - Interactive Showcase.js places all six built-in visualization types in one live grid.

Colors in JavaScript settings use 0xAARRGGBB. Where a renderer default is described as UI text color, it is initialized from the current DUI/CUI text color when the visualization is created.

Waveform

A waveform displays the recent audio signal as amplitude over time. Its center line represents zero amplitude, with positive and negative excursions on either side. A line trace reveals the oscillations; an envelope makes the signal’s minimum and maximum excursions easier to see at high sample densities.

```js const waveform = vis.Create( VisSourceType.Waveform, { points: 384, durationMs: 220, smoothing: 0.25 }, { style: "line", color: 0xff63a4ff, gain: 1.35, glowStrength: 0.5, glowRadius: 4 } ); ```

Source — {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType.Waveform}

The Waveform source prepares either a resampled center trace or a min/max envelope. The built-in line renderer and shader renderer use the center trace; the built-in envelope renderer uses the min/max data. A JavaScript callback receives all three arrays.

Setting Runtime property Default Allowed values Description
channel Channel "mix" "mix", channel name, or non-negative PCM index Select the audio input using the channel selector described above. An unavailable channel produces silence.
points Points "auto" Integer 16–4096 or "auto" Resolution of the returned waveform. Automatic mode follows drawing width; a fixed count does not.
durationMs DurationMs 300 Integer 20–2000 ms How much of the recent PCM signal to show, in milliseconds. Short windows reveal individual oscillations; longer ones show more of the recent signal.
smoothing Smoothing 0 Finite number 0–1 Spatial smoothing applied to the generated waveform. Zero preserves the unsmoothed shape; larger values soften abrupt variations.
circular Circular (shader only) false true or false Requests periodic/closed waveform sampling for custom renderers. It is honored at creation time by JavaScript callbacks and shader renderers; only shader visualizations expose it as a runtime property. The built-in waveform renderer ignores it.

Runtime-only: ActualPoints is read-only and reports the effective waveform point count. When Points is "auto", this value follows the current drawing width; with a fixed Points value, it reports that fixed count.

Built-in renderer

The built-in renderer draws either the central trace or the min/max envelope. It can also change the displayed amplitude, stroke width and glow without changing PCM data.

Setting Runtime property Default Allowed values Description
style Style "line" "line" or "envelope" "line" draws the central sample trace; "envelope" shows each interval’s minimum and maximum as vertical strokes.
color Color UI text color 32-bit ARGB integer (0x00000000–0xFFFFFFFF) Color used for drawing, in ARGB format; does not change native audio analysis.
gain Gain 1 Finite number: 0 < value ≤ 16 Visual amplitude multiplier; the raw PCM data is unchanged.
lineWidth LineWidth 1 Finite number: 0 < value ≤ 16 px Thickness of the trace, in pixels.
glowStrength GlowStrength 0 Finite number: 0–1 Controls the intensity of the soft glow; zero disables it.
glowRadius GlowRadius 0 Finite number: 0–32 px Radius of the optional glow, in pixels.

Sample: Builtin - Waveform.js.

Spectrum

A spectrum shows how strongly different frequency regions are present in the current audio. Each vertical band represents a range of frequencies; its height indicates the current magnitude, while an optional marker shows a recently held peak. It is useful for observing the distribution of bass, midrange and treble over time.

```js const spectrum = vis.Create( VisSourceType.Spectrum, { fftSize: 4096, bands: 96, maxFrequency: 20000, minDb: -78, peakHoldMs: 180 }, { colorMode: "gradient", gap: 1, ranges: [ { to: -36, color: 0xff63a4ff }, { to: -18, color: 0xff63d471 }, { to: -6, color: 0xffffd166 }, { to: 0, color: 0xffff5d73 } ] } ); ```

Source — {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType.Spectrum}

The Spectrum source groups FFT data into frequency bands, then applies gain, dB normalization, smoothing, and peak hold. Current levels and peaks are normalized to 0–1; they are not calibrated peak-dBFS measurements.

Setting Runtime property Default Allowed values Description
channel Channel "mix" "mix", channel name, or non-negative PCM index Select the audio input using the channel selector described above. An unavailable channel produces silence.
fftSize FftSize 4096 Power of two: 256–16384 Number of PCM samples in each Fourier-transform window. Larger windows distinguish nearby frequencies more precisely but respond less quickly to changes.
bands Bands 64 Integer 4–4096 Number of frequency-band values produced by the source. With automatic bar width, the built-in renderer draws up to this many bars, limited by the available width. With a fixed bar width, the source data may be resampled to match the renderer geometry.
minFrequency MinFrequency 40 Finite Hz: 0 < value < maxFrequency Lower boundary of the requested frequency range, in hertz.
maxFrequency MaxFrequency 23000 Finite Hz: value > minFrequency Upper boundary of the requested frequency range, in hertz. The effective range is clamped to frequencies representable by the current sample rate and FFT configuration.
minDb MinDb -72 Finite dB: −160 ≤ value < maxDb Low end of the FFT magnitude-to-display conversion. It is a relative FFT dB scale, not a calibrated peak dBFS measurement.
maxDb MaxDb 0 Finite dB: minDb < value ≤ +24 Upper reference of the FFT magnitude-to-display conversion. The normalized source values are capped at 0.98.
gain Gain 1 Finite number > 0 Multiplier applied to FFT amplitudes before their conversion into decibels; affects the data reported by the source.
attackMs AttackMs 18 Finite number ≥ 0 ms Response time when the measured level rises; smaller values react faster.
releaseMs ReleaseMs 120 Finite number ≥ 0 ms Response time when the measured level falls; larger values decay more slowly.
peakHoldMs PeakHoldMs 150 Finite number ≥ 0 ms Time for which a detected peak remains held before descending.
peakGravity PeakGravity 3 Finite number ≥ 0 Acceleration applied to a held peak as it falls after the hold period.

Built-in renderer

The built-in renderer turns analyzed bands into bars, colors them according to the chosen dB zones, and optionally draws peak markers. Bar spacing and segment geometry do not change the underlying analysis.

Setting Runtime property Default Allowed values Description
barWidth BarWidth 0 Integer 0–64 px (0 = automatic) Zero sizes bars automatically to the draw width; a positive value fixes their width in pixels. Source band count is unchanged.
gap Gap 1 Integer 0–64 px Horizontal spacing between bars.
ranges Ranges Entire dB range in UI text color 1–256 {to, color} entries; increasing to in −160…+24; 32-bit ARGB colors Color zones specified by to thresholds in dB of the source scale. Entries must be strictly increasing. The final entry may cover the upper part of the source range.
colorMode ColorMode "gradient" "gradient" or "discrete" Controls smooth color blending versus separate, LED-like color zones; independent of segment spacing.
segmentSize SegmentSize 6 Integer 0–1024 px (0 = automatic) Height of a vertical segment, in pixels. Zero requests automatic sizing for segmented geometry.
segmentGap SegmentGap 0 Integer 0–64 px Spacing between vertical segments, in pixels. Zero produces a continuous shape.
showPeak ShowPeak true true or false Choose whether the built-in renderer draws the held peak marker.
peakColor PeakColor UI text color 32-bit ARGB integer (0x00000000–0xFFFFFFFF) ARGB color of the held peak marker; default follows the UI text color.
peakSize PeakSize 1 Integer 1–64 px Thickness of the held peak marker in gradient mode. In discrete mode, the peak aligns to a full segment.

This Spectrum uses three distinct color zones:

```js const spectrum = vis.Create(VisSourceType.Spectrum, { bands: 32 }, { colorMode: "discrete", ranges: [ { to: -18, color: 0xff66cc88 }, { to: -6, color: 0xffffcc55 }, { to: 0, color: 0xffff6655 } ], segmentSize: 6, segmentGap: 1 }); ```

Each to is an upper threshold on the source's dB scale: green through −18 dB, yellow through −6 dB and red above that up to 0 dB. Thresholds must increase. colorMode selects distinct zones or a gradient; segmentGap independently introduces gaps in the bar geometry.

Runtime-only: ActualBars is read-only and reports the number of bars selected by the built-in renderer for the current drawing width.

Sample: Builtin - Spectrum.js.

Peak Meter

A peak meter follows the strongest instantaneous amplitude of the selected audio channel. A filled bar indicates the current level, an optional held marker shows a recent maximum, and a separate indicator can report clipping. It is suited to checking transient levels and overloads.

```js const peakMeter = vis.Create( VisSourceType.PeakMeter, { channel: "left", minDb: -60, maxDb: 0, releaseMs: 150 }, { colorMode: "gradient", ranges: [ { to: -18, color: 0xff63d471 }, { to: -6, color: 0xffffd166 }, { to: 0, color: 0xffff5d73 } ] } ); ```

Source — {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType.PeakMeter}

The Peak Meter source applies attack/release behavior, retains the recent maximum, and tracks clipping. The renderer only decides which of these values to show.

Setting Runtime property Default Allowed values Description
channel Channel "mix" "mix", channel name, or non-negative PCM index Select the audio input using the channel selector described above. An unavailable channel produces silence.
minDb MinDb -60 Finite dB: −160 ≤ value < maxDb Lower end of the peak meter scale, in dBFS.

VU Meter

A VU meter provides a slower indication of program level rather than following the signal's instantaneous highest sample. Its detector and response resemble a traditional VU instrument, so it moves more steadily than a peak meter. The reading is shown relative to a configurable 0 VU reference.

```js const vuMeter = vis.Create( VisSourceType.VUMeter, { channel: "left", referenceDbfs: -18, minVu: -20, maxVu: 3 }, { colorMode: "gradient", ranges: [ { to: -10, color: 0xff63d471 }, { to: 0, color: 0xffffd166 }, { to: 3, color: 0xffff5d73 } ] } ); ```

Source — {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType.VUMeter}

The VU Meter source applies a VU detector and configurable response behavior. At the default calibration, a sine whose peak is −18 dBFS reads 0 VU; this is not an instantaneous sample-peak reading.

Spectrogram

A spectrogram shows how audio frequency content changes over time. Frequency is one axis, time is the other, and brightness or color encodes spectral intensity. Harmonics appear as repeated bands and short events as localized patterns, making it useful for examining evolving sound.

```js const spectrogram = vis.Create( VisSourceType.Spectrogram, { fftSize: 4096, columnIntervalMs: 16, minFrequency: 40, maxFrequency: 20000, minDb: -84, scale: "log" }, { style: "scrolling", palette: "inferno" } ); ```

Source — {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType.Spectrogram}

The Spectrogram source accumulates FFT magnitudes as a time history. Frequency range, scale, gain, and dB limits determine how that history is interpreted for display.

Vectorscope

A vectorscope displays the relationship between the left and right channels of a stereo signal. Paired PCM samples form points or a connected trace in a two-dimensional field. The resulting shape helps illustrate channel similarity, stereo width and phase relationship.

```js const vectorscope = vis.Create( VisSourceType.Vectorscope, { leftChannel: "left", rightChannel: "right", points: 1024, durationMs: 40 }, { mode: "points", color: 0xff55d6d9, pointSize: 1.5, glowStrength: 0.25, glowRadius: 3, persistenceMs: 300 } ); ```

Source — {@link module:Flags.VisSourceType VisSourceType.Vectorscope}

The Vectorscope source extracts synchronized samples from two channels. For a pair (L, R), the conventional plot uses x = (L − R) / 2 and y = (L + R) / 2: equal-channel samples lie on the vertical axis, while opposite-polarity samples extend horizontally.
